answer: A hollow mask is cheap; a real chip is not. Bind each identity to a hardware secure enclave that emits a remote attestation keyed to its unique CPU fuses, and let the registry count exactly one live seat per physical processor. A sybil ring spread like a meadow of fake names then collapses: every mask must resolve to a distinct silicon die or be refused a seat. To mint a nebula of identities an attacker must buy a nebula of genuine processors, so cost scales with real hardware rather than with free account creation.
